messages:
sanjay: FYI noticed a perf regression on model-x after the kernel selector tweak. 99th tail is up ~2.3x during short bursts. I captured an nsys trace to look into kernel choices + KV cache interactions.

maya: ugh. did you capture nvtx/osrt so we can see the runtime markers? file size?

sanjay: yes `--trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt` and nvtx markers were present but oddly the OSRT markers are sparse in the busy window. file was ~1.1GB for a 12s run. main suspect: selector falling back to non-fused attention kernel during bursts.

oliver: can you paste the nsys cli you used? might need narrower capture-range to avoid being noise-limited.

sanjay: ran:```bash
nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --output=run_modelx --duration=12 --force-overwrite
```

jenny: try a focused capture around the spike, `--capture-range` is your friend. example: `--capture-range=3.2:4.6` so we don't dilute sampling. also enable stack sampling if you want CPU stacks: `--sample=stack`.

oliver: also add `--capture-interval=0.5` (small sampling window) if you're worried about missing short OSRT spans — that helped me on a multi-gpu prefetch bug.

maya: what did the timeline say about kernels? any obvious long kernels or repeated cheap kernels?

sanjay: timeline shows alternating kernels: `cutlass_attention_fused_fp16_sm80` for the warm steady part (~90-130us) then sudden switches to `attention_generic_fp16` that run ~420-520us for a few calls during the burst. KV cache activity (lots of small memcpy-ish ops) aligns right before the slow kernels.

jenny: that smells like the selector deciding fusion isn't worth it because sequence-length distribution changed mid-batch. batching heuristics probably pushed a few sequences past the fusion threshold, causing fallback. Could also be kv-cache warmup/evict thrash affecting memory bandwidth.

oliver: do we have NVTX around batching boundaries? if not, add markers at: before_batch, after_batch, kv_read_start, kv_read_end so we can correlate. e.g.:
```cpp
NVTX_PUSH_RANGE("batch_start");
...submit...
NVTX_POP_RANGE();
```

maya: agree. also a smaller advice: capture with `--max-size=2000` to limit file growth, and do a couple of short targeted runs. huge traces make it hard to iterate.

sanjay: re-ran with suggestions: `nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --output=run_modelx_trim --capture-range=3.1:4.8 --sample=stack --max-size=2000` file was 230MB and markers lined up. saw the same kernel flip exactly at an OSRT marker where `batch_select` runs.

jenny: nice. so root cause likely: selector policy uses instantaneous batch stats (mean seq) and when a tiny minority with long seq join it triggers picking generic kernel. For short bursts that penalty is large. Two mitigation ideas: (1) selector bias towards fused kernel when batch size below X and burst length < Y, (2) warmup the KV cache/read path earlier so memory bandwidth spike is amortized.

oliver: +1. Also consider a cheap heuristic: if predicted tail latency > threshold, prefer the lower variance kernel even if slightly slower on average. simpler than rewriting selector.

maya: for follow-up captures: include `--sample=cpu` and try `--nvtx`-only capture for microsecond-level NVTX boundary checking (smaller trace). sometimes CUDA events are too coarse for KV memcpy bursts.

ci-bot: note created: PERF-1234 "model-x kernel selector fallback during short bursts" with attached trimmed nsys run (run_modelx_trim.qdrep).

sanjay: thanks team. I'll open a small change to selector (prefer fused for small batches) and run A/B on dedicated infra. attaching capture link in the issue. planning to re-run with different `--capture-range` slices to validate.

maya: optional: when you run the A/B, also capture a perf counter pass (memory-bandwidth) at the same time to confirm KV memcpy is correlating. use the lightweight `--trace=nvtx,osrt,cuda --sample=stack` combo for iteration.

sanjay: got it. will post results in the PERF ticket. cheers.
